newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso signs decree for banking ADRs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso signs decree for banking ADRs.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has signed a decree empowering Brazilian banks to issue stock for trading overseas, including American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), a presidential spokeswoman said Tuesday.
A decree signed by the president late Monday permits the sale of non-voting shares in Brazilian banks overseas and their offering of ADRs, she said.
However, the banks will not be able to engage in foreign trading of their common stock that carry voting rights.
Finance Minister Pedro Malan, in an explanatory note accompanying the decree, said the move was aimed at attracting foreign capital to Brazil's banks which need to invest in new technology.
Malan said the decree did not alter existing rules which restrict foreign banks to a maximum of 30 percent of Brazilian banks' voting shares.
The proposal to allow banks to sell non-voting shares aboard and trade ADRs convertible in non-voting shares was approved by a meeting of the National Monetary Council in October.
